title: Multi-Head Attention with a KV Cache
prompt:
Implement `MHA(n_heads, dim)` with `forward(x, mask=None, kv_cache=None) -> (output, (K, V))`. Use `W_qkv: dim → 3 * dim` and `W_o: dim → dim`. Q comes only from the current input chunk. K and V have shape `(B, n_heads, cached_tokens + T, head_dim)` and append current projected keys/values to the supplied cache along dimension 2. Return only current outputs `(B, T, dim)`. `kv_cache=None` starts a cache; supplied caches have compatible shape, dtype, and device. Do not detach cached tensors or mutate the previous cache.

The caller controls causality: with prefix length P, a causal chunk mask of shape `(T, P + T)` allows key j for query i exactly when `j <= P + i`. A single new token can attend to all cached/current keys without a mask. Scores have shape `(B, n_heads, T, P + T)`.

Use PyTorch on CPU. Preserve the public API and expose biased `nn.Linear` layers named `W_qkv` and `W_o`. Inputs are floating tensors `x: (B, T, dim)` with positive dimensions. Preserve dtype/device and autograd; do not mutate inputs or parameters. No dropout, residual connection, layer normalization, positional encoding, or implicit causal mask is required. `mask` is either None or a boolean tensor broadcastable to attention scores; True means allowed. Every query row has at least one allowed key. Apply the mask before softmax over keys, and scale scores by `1 / sqrt(head_dim)`. Reject nonpositive or nondivisible constructor head/dimension values with AssertionError. Input shapes, mask dtype, and mask rows otherwise satisfy this contract.

example.input: model = MHA(2, 8); first, cache = model(torch.randn(1, 1, 8)); next_out, cache = model(torch.randn(1, 1, 8), kv_cache=cache)
example.reasoning: The second call queries only its new token while attending to both cached and current keys.
